blindSummary:
Trans visitors here face severe risk. A criminal-code provision penalises male same-sex conduct (up to 3 years) — and an international legal-aid organisation notes transgender people may be targeted under it, since there is no legal gender recognition and trans people are legally recorded as their birth sex. There is substantial evidence of recent enforcement: frequent arrests, and extortion by threat of arrest, with police as the most common perpetrators of anti-LGBT violence; torture goes unpunished (an international human-rights organisation). Because the conduct is criminalised, victims cannot report violence to authorities.

A national human-rights group's 2024 report documents continuing rights violations, and the justice ministry denies registration to independent human-rights groups — no community infrastructure can operate openly. There is no documented trans-visitor case, but the legal mechanism (birth-sex status + the criminal-code provision) means a trans visitor discovered in a same-sex-appearing relationship faces direct prosecution risk, and discovery itself invites extortion.
blindOutOfScope: The criminal-code provision formally applies to male same-sex conduct; its application to trans people is via birth-sex legal status — a direct mechanism, not merely climate.

An international human-rights organisation's 2024 world-report chapter on this country: includes a sexual-orientation and gender-identity section amid a deteriorating human-rights record (harassment of online commentators, impunity following a crackdown in a restive autonomous region, constitutional changes).

National human-rights group report (2024) on violations of the rights of LGBT people in this country: legislation, absence of anti-discrimination law, criminalisation of HIV transmission, legal gender recognition, access to human rights, right to health and right to work.
A foreign home ministry's official country-of-origin information and assessment for asylum claims on sexual orientation and gender identity or expression (July 2024).

A foreign government's 2021 human-rights report for this country: official assessment - same-sex conduct criminalised under a criminal-code provision; police abuse and societal stigma; no legal protections.

A foreign government's 2023 human-rights report for this country: official assessment - continued criminalisation under the criminal-code provision, societal discrimination, and no anti-discrimination protections.
International human-rights organisation (March 2021): a report on the abuse, extortion and violence gay men face in prison under prosecutions brought under the criminal-code provision.
blindTangential: The criminal-code provision penalises male same-sex conduct (up to 3 years) — a direct risk for trans visitors with partners or perceived as same-sex-active; extortion-by-threat-of-arrest targets discovered trans people.
